---
title: "Setup & Smoke Test"
subtitle: "Verify the live coding environment works on your device"
---

This page checks that interactive code runs in your browser. **Nothing needs to
be installed on your iPad** — the R and Python engines download once (first
load takes ~10–30 seconds on Wi-Fi) and are cached afterwards.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## First-load tips (iPad Safari)

- Use **Wi-Fi** the first time; the engine download is one-time per site.
- If a cell ever stalls, tap **Restart** (⟳) in the cell toolbar.
- Turn off **Lock** during a session; backgrounding Safari mid-download can
  pause it.
:::

## 1. R smoke test

This cell loads **dplyr and ggplot2** from the WebAssembly R repository and
plots a classic dataset. Press **Run**.

```{webr}
#| label: r-smoke
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

mtcars |>
  group_by(cyl) |>
  summarise(mean_mpg = mean(mpg), n = n())
```

```{webr}
#| label: r-plot
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "If you see this plot, R graphics work")
```

## 2. Python smoke test

This cell uses **pandas** and **matplotlib** (Pyodide engine).

```{pyodide}
#| label: py-smoke
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"cyl": [4, 6, 8], "mean_mpg": [26.66, 19.74, 15.10]})
df
```

```{pyodide}
#| label: py-plot
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 100)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x), label="sin")
plt.plot(x, np.cos(x), label="cos")
plt.legend()
plt.title("If you see this plot, Python graphics work")
plt.show()
```

## 3. Bioinformatics packages in the browser

Biopython runs live in this course:

```{pyodide}
#| label: py-bio
from Bio.Seq import Seq

dna = Seq("ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG")
print(f"Length:       {len(dna)}")
print(f"Reverse comp: {dna.reverse_complement()}")
print(f"Protein:      {dna.translate()}")
```

## 4. Exercise mechanics

Exercises give you a starter, an optional hint, and a collapsible solution.
**Complete the function** so it returns GC content as a percentage, then press
**Run Code** and **Submit Answer**:

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex-gc
gc_content <- function(seq) {
  # Your code here: (number of G + C) / length * 100
  ______
}
gc_content("ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG")
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex-gc"}
Count the `G`s and `C`s with `str_count()` or `grepl`, divide by `nchar(seq)`,
multiply by 100.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="ex-gc"}
```r
gc_content <- function(seq) {
  sum(strsplit(toupper(seq), "")[[1]] %in% c("G", "C")) / nchar(seq) * 100
}
gc_content("ATGGCCATTGTAATGGGCCGCTGAAAGGGTGCCCGATAG")
```
:::

## 5. Report a failure

If any cell above errors, stalls, or never finishes loading:

- Note the **section number** and the **error text**
- Try Safari's *Reload the Page* once
- Tell me (in our session) — the fix is usually a cell option or engine tweak,
  not a change of platform
